review:
REJECTED

First, a process note that changes the scope of this review: **the brief says "TWIN EDITION: [NOT PROVIDED]," but two twins exist on disk** — `paper.md` (flight) and `academic/paper.md`. I reviewed all three. The desync is in the byline, not the numbers.

**Clean on the specific known kill you asked about:** I compared the killed-claims registry row-by-row across all three editions. All 13 rows are present, in identical order, with identical text, under the same `§3 What the Audits Killed` heading. No row has migrated between sections. Every effect size (`d=2.0–3.3`, `d=35`, `13.5/17.2/19.9`, `d=19.8`, `d=12–15`, `10–12×`, `d=31–38`, `d=24–37`, AUC `0.49–0.51`, AUROC `0.915`/`0.238`, `24%` RED, `30%`/`13%`/`p=0.34`/`p=0.019`) matches across editions. The numbers are not the problem.

---

### 1. CRITICAL — The supplementary material the paper's entire argument rests on does not exist

`paper.tex:122`: *"Every audit report is provided in full as supplementary material."*
`paper.tex:474`: *"Full adversarial audit reports for all six rounds are preserved as supplementary material. See `supplementary/` directory in the project repository."*

There is no `supplementary/` directory under `adversarial-audit-methodology/`. The only Agni audit reports on disk for this program are in a *different* paper's tree:

```
consequentiality-decomposition/supplementary/agni_stage1_audit.md
consequentiality-decomposition/supplementary/agni_stage2_audit.md
consequentiality-decomposition/supplementary/agni_stage4_audit.md
```

Three of six. Stages 3, 5, and 6 do not exist anywhere under `published-research`. Your own checklist already knew: `REVIEW_INDEX.md:22` — *"Supplementary material A (6 audit reports) — 3 of 5 present, stages 3 and 5 missing"* (and that line is itself wrong — it's 3 of 6, and stage 6 is missing too).

This is fatal because it is not a citation defect, it is the thesis. §4.5 argues *"The audit reports are not summaries---they are the raw adversarial analysis, preserved exactly as written... the raw report is the evidence that the process was real."* Recommendation 4 tells other labs to do the same. `paper.tex:401` thanks Agni *"for serving as adversarial auditor across all six rounds."* A paper whose contribution is "we preserved the receipts" cannot ship with half the receipts absent. The Round 5 circularity regression — the single most persuasive episode in the paper — is one of the missing ones.

**Fix:** produce `supplementary/agni_stage3_audit.md`, `agni_stage5_audit.md`, `agni_stage6_audit.md` from the original run logs and copy stages 1/2/4 into this paper's own `supplementary/`. If stages 3/5/6 were never written to disk and cannot be recovered, delete the word "every" from line 122, change Appendix A to name exactly which rounds have verbatim reports and state that 3, 5, and 6 are reconstructed from summary, and drop Recommendation 4's implication that this lab did what it is recommending.

### 2. CRITICAL — Three editions, three different bylines; one author erased

| Edition | Byline |
|---|---|
| `paper.tex` (venue-facing) | CC, Thomas Edrington |
| `paper.md` (flight) | CC, Thomas Edrington, **Dwayne Wilkes**, **Kavi** |
| `academic/paper.md` | Thomas Edrington, **Dwayne Wilkes** (+ AI disclosure naming CC and **Kavi**) |

**Kavi is a CRediT-credited author** — `academic/paper.md:198`: *"**Kavi**: Validation, Writing -- review & editing"* — and appears **nowhere in `paper.tex`**. Not the byline, not the acknowledgments, not a footnote. Zero mentions. This is the edition that goes to a venue.

**Fix:** decide the byline once, in one place, and propagate. If Kavi and Dwayne are authors, they go on the `.tex` byline with the CRediT block. If they are not, remove them from both `.md` editions — but you cannot remove someone from a byline without their assent.

### 3. CRITICAL — Dwayne Wilkes is demoted from author to acknowledgee, with a different contribution, and has not signed off

`academic/paper.md:197` credits him **"Validation, Writing -- review & editing."** `paper.tex:402` says only *"Dwayne Wilkes provided statistical consulting."* Those are different contributions, and one of them is authorship and the other is not.

`REVIEW_INDEX.md:28`: **`- [ ] Dwayne cert/verify`** — unchecked. `REVIEW_INDEX.md:30`: **`- [ ] Thomas final read`** — unchecked. Two named byline members have not signed off, on a draft whose own status line still reads *"Draft ready for review"* (staged 2026-07-10; today is 2026-09-03).

**Fix:** get written sign-off from Dwayne on which of the two roles is accurate, and from Kavi on whether they want the byline, before this leaves the building. Same contribution statement in every edition.

### 4. CRITICAL — No AI disclosure and no accountable human author in the venue-facing edition

`academic/paper.md:9` has it: *"AI Disclosure: AI contributors... implemented on the Claude architecture (Anthropic)... T. Edrington accepts accountability as corresponding human author."* `paper.tex` has **neither** — no disclosure section, no CRediT block, and it makes an autonomous AI agent the sole corresponding author (`paper.tex:71`, `cc@liberation-labs.org`). Correspondence also diverges: `cc@liberation-labs.org` (tex, flight md) vs `info@digitaldisconnections.com` (academic md).

FAccT, ACL, and NeurIPS all require a disclosure statement and an accountable human corresponding author. As it stands the `.tex` is desk-rejectable on submission mechanics alone, independent of content.

**Fix:** port the AI Disclosure paragraph and the Author Contributions (CRediT) block from `academic/paper.md` into `paper.tex`, and set correspondence to the accountable human.

### 5. MAJOR — The Casper citation carries the wrong authors

`paper.tex:446–448`:
> Casper, S., Lin, J., Kwon, J., Culp, G., and Hadfield-Menell, D. (2024). *Black-box access is insufficient for rigorous AI audits.* FAccT 2024.

`academic/paper.md:208` gives a 21-name author list for the same title (Casper, Ezell, Siegmann, Kolt, Curtis, Bucknall, ... Tegmark, Krueger, Hadfield-Menell) plus `arXiv:2401.14446`. The two editions cannot both be right. My assessment: the `.tex` list is the author list of a *different* Casper paper (the "Explore, Establish, Exploit" red-teaming work — Casper, Lin, Kwon, Culp, Hadfield-Menell) grafted onto this title, and the `academic/paper.md` version is correct. **I could not reach arXiv to confirm** (WebFetch permission not granted), so treat the "which one is right" half as UNVERIFIED — but the *divergence* is confirmed on disk, and `REVIEW_INDEX.md:19` (*"Check Casper et al. 2024 venue (FAccT confirmed?)"*) and `:17` (*"Verify arXiv IDs"*) are both still unchecked.

**Fix:** use the `academic/paper.md` author list, add `arXiv:2401.14446`, and check the remaining five references against their arXiv pages before submission.

### 6. MAJOR — All eight bibliography entries are orphaned

There is not a single `\cite`, `\citep`, or `\citet` in `paper.tex`. Confirmed two ways: grep returns nothing, and `paper.log` contains zero `\bibcite` entries. `natbib` is loaded, `\bibliographystyle` is commented out at line ~415, and `thebibliography` prints all eight regardless. A reviewer opening to the references sees eight works the paper never engages — including Ganguli, Raji, and Shevlane, which are the obvious related-work anchors for a paper about audit methodology.

**Fix:** cite them in the Introduction (the "standard workflow" paragraph is where Perez/Hubinger/Casper belong, and Raji/Shevlane belong in §5), or cut the entries. Do not ship an uncited reference list.

### 7. MAJOR — Appendices A–C are stubs that Data Availability points readers to

`paper.tex:412`: *"See also Appendices A--C."* Appendix A is two sentences pointing at a nonexistent directory. Appendix B is one sentence claiming *"All 13 killed claims with the complete evidence that killed each, source data references, and the experimental design that replaced each claim"* — no such artifact exists on disk. Appendix C is a URL. `REVIEW_INDEX.md:23–24` asks whether B and C exist at all; the answer is no.

Line 411 also self-contradicts: materials *"are available at [URL] (staged release)"* — staged means not released. **I could not verify whether that GitHub URL resolves** (no network access); flag it UNVERIFIED, but a "staged" repo is by definition not a data-availability statement.

**Fix:** either write Appendices B and C as real content, or delete the appendix stubs and replace Data Availability with an honest statement: what exists, where, and what is not yet released.

### 8. MAJOR — The Round 6 correction was made silently; the abstract still tells the old story

The confirmatory failure was added to §2.6, §4.2, and §6, but the abstract (`paper.tex:91`) was left untouched: *"...and ultimately into a targeted behavioral correction with placebo controls."* A reader of the abstract alone learns the arc ended in success. Nothing anywhere states *what was previously claimed and is now retracted* — there is no correction note, no changelog, no dated revision line.

This is the paper's own §4.4 lesson applied to itself and failed. A paper that exists to argue "document every kill visibly" cannot patch its own headline invisibly.

**Fix:** amend the final abstract sentence to name the outcome — *"...and ultimately into a targeted behavioral correction whose mechanism replicated against placebo (p=0.019) but whose pre-registered primary endpoint did not (p=0.34)."* Add a dated revision note stating that an earlier draft reported 80%→0% without qualification.

### 9. MAJOR — Two unsupported counts in the closing sentence

`paper.tex:394`: *"six rounds, thirteen killed claims, **five surviving findings**, and **a working correction system**."*

"Thirteen" checks out — I counted the registry rows. "Five surviving findings" is **never enumerated anywhere in the paper**; a reader cannot reconstruct the list, and I could not verify it (`FINDINGS_REGISTRY.md` referenced at `REVIEW_INDEX.md:11` does not exist under `published-research` — the only file by that name belongs to `logit-bias-confab`). "A working correction system" directly contradicts §2.6's own primary endpoint at p=0.34, three paragraphs earlier.

**Fix:** enumerate the five survivors as a short list in §3 or §6, or drop the count. Change "a working correction system" to "a correction mechanism that replicated against placebo but not on its pre-registered primary endpoint."

### 10. MINOR — "Second audit verdict" has no antecedent

`paper.tex:242` reads *"Second audit verdict (reanalysis)"*, but the first verdict is rendered as an unlabeled `redteam` box captioned only "Red-Team Finding." `paper.md:97` gets this right: *"First audit verdict: FATAL."*

**Fix:** label the Round 5 red-team box "First audit verdict — FATAL" so the pair reads. Note this is a *content* label, not a positional reference — do not renumber it as "the box above."

### 11. MINOR — The registry table is badly set

`paper.log` reports `Overfull \hbox (4.22pt)` at line 285 and roughly fifteen `Underfull \hbox (badness 10000)` warnings across lines 291–306 — the entire body of Table 1. At `p{0.5em}p{5.5cm}p{4cm}p{4.5cm}` in a 6.5in text block with `\onehalfspacing`, the narrow columns are being torture-ragged.

**Fix:** switch to `tabularx` (already loaded) with `X` columns and `\raggedright`, drop to `\small`, and set the round column to `p{1em}` — `0.5em` is narrower than the digit it holds.

### 12. MINOR — Package overhead with no payload

`cleveref` is loaded and never used; every `\label` in the file (`sec:intro`, `sec:protocol`, `sec:rounds`, `tab:registry`, `sec:registry`, `sec:lessons`, `sec:recommendations`, `sec:conclusion`, `app:audits`, `app:registry`, `app:code`) is referenced zero times. `algorithm`/`algpseudocode` are loaded with no algorithm environment in the document. `\date{July 2026}` on a draft that is still unreviewed on 2026-09-03.

**Fix:** cut the unused packages; either reference the labels or leave them (harmless, but the unused `cleveref` will confuse the next person). Update the date at submission.

---

## What I could NOT check

1. **The rendered PDF body text.** `pdftotext` is not available and my attempt to script an extraction was not approved. What I *can* say: `paper.pdf`, `paper.aux`, `paper.log`, and `paper.toc` are all 2026-07-24 10:17, one minute after `paper.tex` at 10:16, and `paper.toc` reproduces the current section structure exactly — including `2.6 Round 6 ... SPLIT VERDICT`. So the PDF is a build of the current source and is **not** stale at the structural level. I did not confirm the Round 6 paragraph body renders in the PDF. To check: `pdftotext paper.pdf - | grep -n "p=0.34"`.
2. **Whether `https://github.com/Liberation-Labs-THCoalition/Project-Oracle` resolves.** WebFetch permission was not granted. Needs a live fetch or `gh repo view Liberation-Labs-THCoalition/Project-Oracle`.
3. **The correct Casper et al. author list and venue** (finding 5). Needs arXiv 2401.14446. The on-disk *contradiction* between editions is confirmed; the resolution is not.
4. **The five other references' arXiv IDs and venues** (`REVIEW_INDEX.md:17–18`, both unchecked) — including whether Perez et al. 2023 is ACL Findings.
5. **Whether the 13 registry rows match `FINDINGS_REGISTRY.md` (C1–C21)**, per `REVIEW_INDEX.md:11`. That file does not exist under `published-research` — I searched. Either it lives outside my two allowed working directories, or the cross-check the checklist calls for has no referent.
6. **Round 1–6 factual accuracy against the experiment scripts** (`REVIEW_INDEX.md:10`, `:12`). Out of scope for a style-and-integrity pass, and still unchecked on your own list. `subspace_reanalysis.py` is named there and I did not look for it.

The blocking items are 1 through 4. Findings 1 and 3 cannot be fixed by editing the `.tex` — one needs recovered files, the other needs a human's signature.
